I like how the doors add warmth to otherwise minimal spaces; details like this are what make interiors feel lived-in. When I’m working on interior scenes, I think about the same balance you’d use when styling a real room, whether it’s doors, furniture, or even a dining table runner set that ties a space together without overdoing it. Clean, simple assets like these make that kind of visual harmony much easier to achieve.

I've been seeing a lot of confusion and disingenuine answers regarding the state of this account, so for all who might require it, here is my take on the situation of this account.

Although the profile picture is definitely generated at the Slop Factory, the models aren't. Their topology is too neat and optimised, as are the textures, which is proof of professional work.
The numbering in the names points to the file size which is handy for those who want to manage the size of their project, especially prevalent in the field of Game Development where you not only have to store the assets, but also have other people download them.

At the start of this account's upload history, you can see some assets with Arabian names and iconography. Considering the name of the account also sounds rather arabian, these may in fact be their own creations, further supported by the fact that they are some of the only textures that have AI-generated textures on them.

That era ends swiftly, however, as the uploaded models then proceed to take on the same theme, style, quality and density, with loads of models published in just one week. Some time later, a different theme and style, and so on, eventually even showing copyrighted characters that any videogame enjoyer will recognise. This all leads me to conclude that this channel does not post original content, but instead makes gamerips and puts them online to create some mismatched archive of generic-looking gameripped assets.

This leads me to believe that the reason for this account's sudden stop in posting, is copyright infringement strikes. While I don't know whether they've lost access to the account, it is clear they've stopped posting in fear of a strike that may get this archive deleted.

On the non-zero chance that I am completely and utterly incorrect, instead of being told to eat a dick or somesuch, I invite the owner of this account to update their profile with proof of intellectual property, or some spot in the credits of the games these assets belong to, and to provide a more complete description to your posts in the future.


Thank you for reading.

According to this agreement, Egypt agreed to provide several Soviet-made aircraft to the United States for research, in exchange for the US providing some other military equipment to Egypt. The MiG-19S with serial number 0138 was one of the aircraft that Egypt transferred to the United States under this arrangement.

After being transferred to the US, the MiG-19S underwent thorough evaluation and testing by US Air Force experts to gather information about its design, features, and combat capabilities. This information was extremely valuable, helping the United States better understand the air power of its adversary in the context of the tense Cold War.

Grass: select it and go to the inspector tab find the Mesh>Surface Materials section, click on the material slot and select "New StandardMaterial3D click the new material to edit it, set Albedo>Color to your desired color i recommend #3A7D3A for low poly grass.

Water: same as grass select water surface material slot and add a New StandardMaterial3D and set Albedo>Color to bluish i recommend #3AB4F2 or #5577FF for low poly water, set Transparency>Mode to Alpha or Blend as you wish, set Refraction to 0.05 or 0.2 for effects, set Roughness to 0.1 or 0.3 for a bit of shine, and set Metallic to 0.0.

How do you make flowers like this? I'm trying to learn

@emlie sorry for late response, missed your comment （；´д｀）ゞ

To put it straight:
1. Get references of what you plan to make (photos, drawings)
2. Decide on target optimization level (just billboard, main parts as mesh and cards, full details as mesh)
3. Model necessary parts (flower/petals, leaves, stem). Usually I make base model in blender, then sculpt form to get good highpoly for bake.
4. Bake your part to texture, you will get Normal, Opacity. (also cavity, etc if needed) You can bake in blender or take to marmoset/painter/other.
5. Bring texture to painter (or other texturing software) to add color, more details in normal, roughness.
Here you should have texture set for your plant.
6. Now we can start assembling final model. I usually do it in speedtree, as it makes creation of LODs much easier, has all the tools for plant creation (generators, curves, cards cut out, etc). But you can still go with blender - more control, yet LODs will require manual work and billboards will be one more round of texture baking.
Here you should have a final model and LODs. (or just a model, or just billboards, depending on your target)

If you want to practice, good idea will be to create something stylized with just albedo and opacity. You can create both textures together in photoshop/blender texture paint/Krita. Basically put you straight to point 6. Plus, you can go with just lowpoly model with no extra LODs and billboards, to try different approaches - almost any type of plant/flower will need a little different setup.

Hope that helps!
